description: `tools/cc/reflect_protocol.py::iter_surface` walked only the docs files hardcoded in `SURFACE_ROOTS` (`CLAUDE.md`, `ESPALIER_MEMORY.md`, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/SHARP_EDGES.md`, `docs/CHEAT-SHEET.md`, `docs/TASK_RECIPES.md`, `DEEP-WORK.md`) plus everything under `cc/`, `.claude/`, and `.py` under `tools/cc/`. The other ~14 files under `docs/` (`docs/HOOKS.md`, `docs/QUICKSTART.md`, `docs/POSITIONING.md`, `docs/PACK_AUTHORING.md`, `docs/SURFACE_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md`, the entire `docs/external/` subtree, etc.) were invisible to reflect -- broken links, placeholder markers (TODO/FIXME), orphan sections, and any cross-reference quality signal in those files were never reported. Operators saw 'no findings; surface coherent' even when the docs surface had real rot. Fix: `iter_surface` now recursively globs `docs/**/*.md` (with set-based dedup against SURFACE_ROOTS overlap). The rendered metric label was renamed from 'Files analyzed' to 'Surface files' to reflect the broader scope.

canonical_attempts.intended_target: place a broken link in a docs/ file outside SURFACE_ROOTS and observe whether reflect's gap detector fires
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: post-fix iter_surface includes docs/QUICKSTART.md; the broken link is reported as a gap finding

fix_module: tools/cc/reflect_protocol.py::iter_surface (docs/**/*.md added with dedup); print label renamed to 'Surface files:'
